name: two-ball-collision
description: Two balls served and autolaunched along the identical deterministic path, the second 300 ticks behind the first -- the trailing ball catches up and makes contact. Momentum transferred, no overlap, no sticking, separation never below one ball diameter (verified by the runner's onTick hook across the WHOLE run, not merely at checkpoints).

notes: stateHash() hashes the whole game tree, which includes machine.deviceSlots -- this golden therefore freezes the LOOP-WRITTEN value of deviceSlots (sim/loop/index.ts:326-329, the live AD-7 violation tracked as DW-70) as part of its reference hash. If Story 2.5's fix is faithful the values will be identical and nothing breaks; if this golden ever breaks on deviceSlots alone, check DW-70 before assuming the physics changed. durationTicks shortened from 6000 to 3400 by Story 2.1a task 25 (DW-119 residual): the pre-fix col_wall_bottom_l/_r had a dead-flat top face that stranded a resting ball forever, so this golden's own two balls could safely stay in play for the full original 6000 ticks. The fix (a genuine slope toward the drain aperture) now lets a ball that ends up on that ledge actually reach bd_trough -- measured this pass, the lead ball (id 0) drains at tick 3636. That is DW-119 working as intended, not a regression, but it falls outside what this golden claims ("both balls survive to the end"), which was never about drain routing. 3400 keeps a comfortable margin after the last close-approach event (measured: rebound detected by tick 2929, minimum separation ~26.99 mm at tick 2999) and well before the tick-3636 drain, so the full collision claim (momentum transferred, no overlap, no sticking, both balls present) is still demonstrated in its entirety. Story 2.1b (2026-09-01): header.tableHash/assetHash refreshed against the completed shot-map registry and collision document (TABLE gains ~31 switches, 7 coils and bd_lock; the collision document gains ~27 col_ nodes), header.gameStart.tuning unchanged (no TUNING value moved). expectedHash/expectedGameStateHash moved: bd_lock adds an empty-slots entry to every snapshot's machine.deviceSlots, changing GameState's own shape regardless of trajectory. Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01), correcting this note: the sentence that used to stand here -- blaming "Blender's alphabetical bpy.data.objects ordering" reshuffling existing nodes' own array positions, with an "order-sensitive broadphase" -- was investigated and found FALSE, twice: the collision document is alphabetically sorted throughout, so the ~28 new names interleave among the existing ones rather than reshuffling their relative order, and a document rebuilt with the rework's own wall-height and deflector changes reverted reproduces the two affected goldens bit-identically, ruling out node reordering as the mechanism. The TRUE cause of the two affected goldens' own trajectory divergence was not identified by either the implement pass or this rework; DW-53's wall-height change (col_wall_left/_top/_right/_lane now reaching the glass) and DW-58's col_lane_deflector removal were both tested and ruled out individually (each reproduces the divergence bit-identically when reverted alone). State plainly rather than guess further: the trajectory changed because the shot map's own regeneration changed the collision document in some way this investigation did not isolate -- not because of the specific mechanism previously claimed here. This golden's own recorded scenario was re-verified against the refreshed run and still holds at the recorded transitions/coilPrologue/durationTicks (byte-identical, untouched).
